summary: The Great Turkish War, also called the War of the Holy League, was a series of conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and the Holy League, which included the Habsburg Monarchy, Poland-Lithuania, Venice and Russia. Intensive fighting began in 1683 and ended with the Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699. The Ottomans suffered a defeat in which, for the first time, they lost large amounts of territory, including lands in Hungary, the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and part of the western Balkans. The note also highlights that the war marked Russia's first involvement in a western European alliance.
one_line: The Great Turkish War (1683–1699) was a conflict in which the Ottoman Empire, fighting the Holy League, lost large territories under the Treaty of Karlowitz.
key_facts: The Great Turkish War is also called the War of the Holy League.
The war was a series of conflicts between the Ottoman Empire and the Holy League.
The Holy League consisted of the Habsburg Monarchy, Poland-Lithuania, Venice and Russia.
Intensive fighting in the Great Turkish War began in 1683.
The Great Turkish War ended with the signing of the Treaty of Karlowitz in 1699.
The war was a defeat for the Ottoman Empire.
The Ottoman Empire lost large amounts of territory for the first time in the Great Turkish War.
The Ottoman Empire lost lands in Hungary as a result of the Great Turkish War.
The Ottoman Empire lost lands in the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth as a result of the Great Turkish War.
The Ottoman Empire lost part of the western Balkans as a result of the Great Turkish War.
The Great Turkish War was the first time Russia was involved in a western European alliance.
